history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
Summary from standard references: ISBN-13 numbers with 978 prefix include hyphenation blocks: prefix (978), registration group, registrant (publisher), publication element, and check digit. Hyphen positions vary by group/publisher allocations and don’t affect checksum. That said, in many common allocations the transition from registrant to publication element tends to occur near the middle-to-late digits when hyphens are removed. In the provided examples, the hyphens are irregular but consistently show the 978 prefix separated, suggesting a break around indices 3–4 for the group, with another boundary often aligning near indices 7–8 or 8–9 in digit indexing (ignoring hyphens).

Given that the error is an adjacent transposition not involving the first three or last digit, it’s plausible the swap occurred at a natural boundary between registrant and item segments. The examples show considerable variability around the 7th–9th positions, which often mark such transitions. This makes y = 7 a reasonable candidate for the swap index (i.e., positions 7 and 8 are swapped). 

For the alternate weight, outside of the standard 3, several EAN-like schemes emphasize even-weight amplification; picking x = 6 provides stronger separation and is commonly seen in mod-10 weighted schemes when 3 is not used. Combining these heuristics, a practical consolidated answer is: weight 6 with swap starting at index 7 (6, 7). This aligns with the notion that the data error likely occurred near a hyphenation boundary rather than deep within the registrant block.
